h1: The portfolio has hooks, not a demand winner
room_line: URANG BUNIAN remains first for its specific local-fit test; AKAL IMITASI ranks second because its concentrated school-and-cast signal carries a group-conversion trap; TABOO remains third with publicity but no usable social or purchase proof.
coming_kick: AKAL IMITASI recorded 53,054 TikTok views across four samples; separately, individual sampled posts reached up to 3,633 for URANG BUNIAN and 3,076 for ISTIMEWA. These aggregate and single-post observations are not comparable measures of relative reach or demand.
coming_caveat: Those samples and overlapping pages are not like-for-like corroborations. None establishes presales, paid demand, private eligibility or booking.
signal_note: TABOO's articles establish identity, publicity and reported cultural controversy—not presales, commercial impact or an independent finished-film verdict.

eligibility.basis: Indonesian-language title and synopsis with Indonesian cast, director, producer and writer; listed by M-Tix inside the operating window.

coming.meta: T Rifnu Wikana, Tika Bravani, DL Entertainment: Zhaddam Aldhy Nurdin directs the child-led ensemble, including Zaskya Alya Kyla and Muhammad Arziqy Herdi Pratama.
coming.logline: A disadvantaged student and her friends confront an unequal AI-powered school system and defend the human values technology cannot replace.
coming.quality: Weak-to-middling quality signal: the only captured independent viewer response scores it 5/10, criticizing cringe writing while finding its plot and acting better than comparable films.
coming.gold: School-community niche: its Semua Umur rating, 98-minute runtime and education-versus-AI premise fit student, teacher and parent group viewing better than a proven mass-market theatrical proposition.
coming.promo: Active but narrow campaign: recent cast-game content and school-viewing posts are visible, yet no captured ticket offer, chain-wide roadshow or conversion mechanism proves opening demand.
coming.social: Concentrated social activity: four relevant TikTok samples total 53,054 views, led by one 36,157-view cast clip; the content is campaign- and school-led, not representative ticket intent.
coming.demand: Ticket demand remains unknown: three Makassar XXI listings show one 16:45 session each on September 17, but no captured presales, seat occupancy, sold-out evidence or SAMS bookings measure intent.
coming.risk: Conversion risk: institutional school circulation and cast-led engagement may look stronger than organic walk-up demand, while the sole independent review flags weak writing and only middling quality.
coming.bet: School and family interest will create isolated group-led pockets, but organic admissions per show will remain weak chain-wide.
coming.nug: Its clearest edge is a timely education-versus-AI premise suited to school communities; whether that converts beyond groups is unproven.

lanes.read: AI disrupts an Indonesian primary school: a disadvantaged student and her friends confront an unequal learning system and defend the human values technology cannot replace.
lanes.strongest_available_evidence: The captured Film Indonesia synopsis directly describes PIKO, unequal premium access, Ika's struggle and the threat surrounding Rafi.
lanes.decision_consequence: Treat it as a clear family-education drama with an accessible topical hook, while avoiding any assumption that topicality creates demand.

lanes.read: Recognizable adult anchors T Rifnu Wikana and Tika Bravani support a child-led ensemble; Zhaddam Aldhy Nurdin directs for DL Entertainment.
lanes.strongest_available_evidence: The captured listings name T Rifnu Wikana, Tika Bravani and the child ensemble, while a fetched production report identifies DL Entertainment and the director.
lanes.decision_consequence: Cast offers some credibility for parents, but no captured evidence supports treating the ensemble as an opening-weekend demand engine.

lanes.read: Weak-to-middling quality signal: the only captured independent viewer response scores it 5/10, criticizing cringe writing while finding its plot and acting better than comparable films.
lanes.strongest_available_evidence: One readable Letterboxd review provides a direct current-film reaction, but it is a single opinion rather than a representative quality sample.
lanes.decision_consequence: Treat the lone 5/10 viewer response as a warning about execution, then test whether paid audience reaction confirms or contradicts that weak-to-middling quality signal.

lanes.read: School-community niche: its Semua Umur rating, 98-minute runtime and education-versus-AI premise fit student, teacher and parent group viewing better than a proven mass-market theatrical proposition.
lanes.strongest_available_evidence: The fetched listing confirms a family-accessible rating and runtime, while captured TikTok posts show school viewing activity around the film.
lanes.decision_consequence: At owner-confirmed eligible booked sites, separate school or community bookings from organic paid attendance to learn whether the education hook travels beyond organized groups.

lanes.read: Active but narrow campaign: recent cast-game content and school-viewing posts are visible, yet no captured ticket offer, chain-wide roadshow or conversion mechanism proves opening demand.
lanes.strongest_available_evidence: A September 12 cast game reached 11,659 views, while two September 6–7 posts documented school-viewing activity.
lanes.decision_consequence: Interpret the campaign as targeted awareness only; the commercial question is whether that activity converts into paid admissions rather than remaining promotional circulation.

lanes.read: Concentrated social activity: four relevant TikTok samples total 53,054 views, led by one 36,157-view cast clip; the content is campaign- and school-led, not representative ticket intent.
lanes.strongest_available_evidence: The four captured TikTok samples total 53,054 views, 3,050 likes, 115 comments and 289 shares, with most reach concentrated in one cast clip.
lanes.decision_consequence: Use the social evidence to define a youth- and school-facing signal, then test whether its campaign-led attention converts into organic paid behavior.

lanes.read: Ticket demand remains unknown: three Makassar XXI listings show one 16:45 session each on September 17, but no captured presales, seat occupancy, sold-out evidence or SAMS bookings measure intent.
lanes.strongest_available_evidence: The fetched schedule page lists one September 17 session at each of M`TOS XXI, PANAKKUKANG and TSM XXI, establishing availability rather than sales.
lanes.missing_fact: D-1 and Day-1 SAMS advance sales, occupied seats, group bookings and admissions per show across the 16 owned sites.
lanes.decision_consequence: The governed exploration floor is evidence collection, not a demand forecast or ceiling; conclusions must come from transaction-level behavior at genuinely eligible booked sites.

lanes.read: Conversion risk: institutional school circulation and cast-led engagement may look stronger than organic walk-up demand, while the sole independent review flags weak writing and only middling quality.
lanes.strongest_available_evidence: Captured social activity is largely promotional or school-linked, and the only readable independent review rates the film 5/10 with explicit writing criticism.
lanes.decision_consequence: The decisive learning is whether site-level organic sales remain weak after group and campaign activity are separated from public demand.

ai_rating.source_confidence: Strong identity and premise evidence; quality rests on one independent viewer review.
ai_rating.sams_relevance: Eligible local release with a school-and-family angle; private booking confirmation is absent.
ai_rating.demand_proximity: Three Makassar sessions establish availability, not presales, occupancy or SAMS demand.
ai_rating.promo_social_strength: 53,054 TikTok views across four samples, concentrated in cast- and school-led content.
ai_rating.risk_pressure: Campaign and group activity may overstate walk-up demand; the sole review scores it 5/10.
ai_rating.actionability: Measure organic versus group admissions on Day 1 and Day 4 before drawing a commercial conclusion.

eligibility.basis: Indonesian-language title and synopsis with Indonesian cast, director, producer and writers; listed by M-Tix inside the operating window.

coming.meta: Mathias Muchus and Kairos Pictures: Ajil Ditto and Agus Kuncoro support the cast; Ruben Adrian directs, Abdullah Mansuri produces, and the film opens September 17.
coming.logline: Five children with disabilities leave Rumah Istimewa to find their ailing foster father, testing whether friendship and acceptance can sustain them as a family.
coming.quality: Warm and sincere, not independently validated: captured material consistently promises family drama, humor and humane disability representation, but no readable independent review tests execution.
coming.gold: Distinctive inclusive family drama, but likely niche-led: authentic disabled protagonists and an all-ages emotional premise create community relevance without proving broad theatrical pull.
coming.promo: Active but message-led campaign: an official trailer, multi-city cinema visits and an XXI Epicentrum gala establish organized outreach, without quantified reach or conversion evidence.
coming.social: Small and noisy social footprint: three clearly film-relevant TikTok samples drew 1,739–3,076 views, 19–123 likes and only 1–3 comments, with no purchase-intent evidence.
coming.demand: Theatrical availability is visible, but purchase demand is unproven: TIX ID carried a release article, while no captured source exposes saleable schedules, seat maps, paid sales or sell-through.
coming.risk: Conversion risk is the decisive concern: a 119-minute mission-led drama has modest sampled interaction and no verified ticket signal, so supportive sentiment may not become paid attendance.
coming.bet: ISTIMEWA will remain below comparable local-new-release admits per show through Day 4.
coming.nug: Authentic disabled protagonists give this all-ages family drama a distinctive community edge, but not yet proven broad theatrical pull.

lanes.read: Five children with disabilities leave Rumah Istimewa to find their ailing foster father, testing whether friendship and acceptance can sustain them as a family.
lanes.strongest_available_evidence: TMDB’s captured overview names Aldo, Bimo, Ken, Nita and Mul and describes their search for the foster father who left after a cancer diagnosis.
lanes.decision_consequence: Treat this as an accessible family-emotion proposition with a clear human hook, not as an abstract issue film.

lanes.read: Mathias Muchus leads the commercially familiar cast for Kairos Pictures, alongside Ajil Ditto and Agus Kuncoro; Ruben Adrian directs and Abdullah Mansuri produces.
lanes.strongest_available_evidence: The captured trailer-release article identifies Kairos Film, director Ruben Adrian, producer Abdullah Mansuri and a cast including Mathias Muchus, Ajil Ditto and Agus Kuncoro.
lanes.decision_consequence: The recognizable adult ensemble adds credibility, but the package lacks a proven mass-audience star capable of overriding weak demand evidence.

lanes.read: Warm and sincere, not independently validated: captured material consistently promises family drama, humor and humane disability representation, but no readable independent review tests execution.
lanes.strongest_available_evidence: Gala coverage documents the intended character treatment and filmmakers’ emphasis on agency rather than pity, but remains premiere and participant material rather than an independent quality verdict.
lanes.missing_fact: A readable independent critic review or clearly independent post-screening audience assessment of acting, pacing and emotional execution.
lanes.decision_consequence: Treat the promised warmth and sincerity as unvalidated until paid audience response shows that the emotional proposition lands in practice.

lanes.read: Distinctive inclusive family drama, but likely niche-led: authentic disabled protagonists and an all-ages emotional premise create community relevance without proving broad theatrical pull.
lanes.strongest_available_evidence: The film centers disabled performers in a 119-minute all-ages family drama based on stories gathered from disability communities.
lanes.decision_consequence: At owner-confirmed eligible booked sites, test whether paid occupancy reaches beyond advocacy and community audiences rather than treating inclusive relevance as broad demand.

lanes.read: Active but message-led campaign: an official trailer, multi-city cinema visits and an XXI Epicentrum gala establish organized outreach, without quantified reach or conversion evidence.
lanes.strongest_available_evidence: Okezone’s captured gala report states that the September 7 premiere followed cinema visits in multiple cities.
lanes.decision_consequence: Count the campaign as useful awareness support only; no readable captured source proves ticket conversion or a BOGOF offer.

lanes.read: Small and noisy social footprint: three clearly film-relevant TikTok samples drew 1,739–3,076 views, 19–123 likes and only 1–3 comments, with no purchase-intent evidence.
lanes.strongest_available_evidence: The captured five-result sample contains three identifiable film posts; one result is unrelated to the film and another has only an emoji, limiting interpretation.
lanes.decision_consequence: Interpret the small, shallow social sample as modest directional awareness and test whether any of it converts into paid attendance.

lanes.read: Theatrical availability is visible, but purchase demand is unproven: TIX ID carried a release article, while no captured source exposes saleable schedules, seat maps, paid sales or sell-through.
lanes.strongest_available_evidence: TIX ID’s captured homepage featured ISTIMEWA and confirmed its September 17 theatrical release, but contained no title-level transaction evidence.
lanes.missing_fact: Site-level advance schedules, paid-ticket counts, seat-map movement or sold-out sessions attributable to ISTIMEWA.
lanes.decision_consequence: The governed exploration floor is a learning mechanism, not a demand forecast or ceiling; Day-1 occupancy and admissions per show must establish the commercial signal.

lanes.read: Conversion risk is the decisive concern: a 119-minute mission-led drama has modest sampled interaction and no verified ticket signal, so supportive sentiment may not become paid attendance.
lanes.strongest_available_evidence: The film’s runtime is 119 minutes, while the relevant captured TikTok posts show low comment depth and no observable ticket-intent language.
lanes.decision_consequence: The commercial test is whether paid behavior materializes quickly; goodwill, representation value and campaign activity are not substitutes for audience demand.

ai_rating.source_confidence: Strong identity and campaign evidence; no independent review or private booking confirmation.
ai_rating.sams_relevance: Eligible local release publicly listed by M-Tix; listing does not confirm private eligibility or booking.
ai_rating.demand_proximity: TIX ID's September 8 article confirms release, not schedules, paid sales, seat movement or sell-through.
ai_rating.promo_social_strength: Official trailer, city visits and September 7 gala; relevant TikToks reached 1,739–3,076 views with 1–3 comments.
ai_rating.risk_pressure: 119-minute drama plus shallow interaction raises conversion risk; supportive sentiment may not become paid attendance.
ai_rating.actionability: Day-1 occupancy and admits per show can test conversion; no captured source proves presales or a BOGOF offer.

eligibility.basis: The capture shows Korean directors, producers, writers and principal tourists alongside Indonesian cast and a Bali/Nyepi setting, but provides no country or production-origin field sufficient to establish local-title eligibility.

coming.meta: Kwon Da-ham, Della Dartyan, Sujiwo Tejo and Showbox: cross-border supernatural horror directed by Park Kyung-kun, with Choi Tae-eun and Lee Jeong-hoon; Indonesian local-title eligibility remains unresolved.
coming.logline: Korean tourists violate Nyepi restrictions in Bali and become trapped with the spirits their actions release.
coming.quality: Atmospheric promise, not a quality verdict: publicity describes slow psychological tension, while no captured critic or post-screening audience review evaluates the finished film.
coming.gold: Distinctive but polarizing hook: Korean horror mechanics placed inside Bali's Nyepi observance may create curiosity while narrowing appeal among viewers sensitive to cultural treatment.
coming.promo: Visible publicity footprint, limited campaign proof: a trailer, Showbox FilMart listing and reported BIFAN premiere exist, but no captured Indonesian roadshow, ticket offer or cinema activation does.
coming.social: No usable title-specific social signal: the single TikTok keyword sample for TABOO returned generic, multilingual and unrelated posts rather than evidence about this film.
coming.demand: Release-date reporting without purchase proof: one recent page states September 17, but the bundle contains no presales, paid-seat evidence, sold-out sessions or title-specific ticket intent.
coming.risk: Cultural-sensitivity risk is specific but unquantified: articles report criticism that using sacred Nyepi observance as a horror device is insensitive or misleading.
coming.bet: If eligible and ticketed, the Nyepi horror hook will spark curiosity, but conversion may trail peers amid sensitivity concerns.
coming.nug: Nyepi is both the title's distinctive hook and its fault line: reported controversy may produce curiosity, rejection or only article-level noise.

lanes.read: Cross-border supernatural horror: Korean tourists violate Nyepi restrictions in Bali and become trapped with the spirits their actions release.
lanes.strongest_available_evidence: Multiple readable articles consistently identify the Bali/Nyepi setting, Korean tourists and supernatural consequences.
lanes.decision_consequence: The room can recognize a culturally specific horror premise, while treating publicity descriptions as identity evidence rather than proof of appeal.

lanes.read: Recognizable cross-border package: Showbox is the reported producer, led by Kwon Da-ham with Della Dartyan, Sujiwo Tejo, Choi Tae-eun and Lee Jeong-hoon.
lanes.strongest_available_evidence: Readable coverage consistently connects Park Kyung-kun and Showbox with Korean and Indonesian cast members.
lanes.decision_consequence: Talent and Showbox provide a credible identity hook, but neither source-IP reputation nor Indonesian cast participation resolves local-title eligibility.

lanes.read: Atmospheric promise, not a quality verdict: publicity describes slow psychological tension, while no captured critic or post-screening audience review evaluates the finished film.
lanes.strongest_available_evidence: Katadata reports a BIFAN premiere, but the readable sources offer synopsis and promotional characterization rather than independent evaluation.
lanes.missing_fact: An independent review or attributable audience response from a completed screening of the current film.
lanes.decision_consequence: Do not convert festival presence, Showbox reputation or favorable article language into a quality judgment; Monday remains observation and learning.

lanes.read: Distinctive but polarizing hook: Korean horror mechanics placed inside Bali's Nyepi observance may create curiosity while narrowing appeal among viewers sensitive to cultural treatment.
lanes.strongest_available_evidence: The premise is repeatedly framed around Nyepi, while readable coverage also reports objections that the sacred observance is being used insensitively.
lanes.decision_consequence: Treat cultural specificity as the strongest adjacent commercial signal, but keep the title unresolved until eligibility and real audience response are known.

lanes.read: Visible publicity footprint, limited campaign proof: a trailer, Showbox FilMart listing and reported BIFAN premiere exist, but no captured Indonesian roadshow, ticket offer or cinema activation does.
lanes.strongest_available_evidence: Readable coverage reports the trailer release, Showbox sales listing and festival premiere; the official trailer asset was uploaded August 7, 2026.
lanes.decision_consequence: Record organized publicity and festival positioning, but do not interpret them as current campaign scale, audience quality or ticket conversion.

lanes.read: No usable title-specific social signal: the single TikTok keyword sample for TABOO returned generic, multilingual and unrelated posts rather than evidence about this film.
lanes.strongest_available_evidence: Ten captured TikTok results were unrelated to TABOO: The Silent Day; the official trailer capture contained no views, likes or comments.
lanes.missing_fact: A title-disambiguated social sample or official-post metrics containing attributable film discussion, engagement and watch intent.
lanes.decision_consequence: Social awareness, engagement and sentiment must remain unscored; the noisy keyword sample cannot move the room's judgment.

lanes.read: Release-date reporting without purchase proof: one recent page states September 17, but the bundle contains no presales, paid-seat evidence, sold-out sessions or title-specific ticket intent.
lanes.strongest_available_evidence: Katadata states an Indonesian theatrical date of September 17, 2026; no readable source supplies a ticket transaction or advance-booking measure.
lanes.missing_fact: Verified presale volume, paid bookings, seat maps or opening-session admissions tied specifically to TABOO.
lanes.decision_consequence: Public listing and release-date coverage cannot establish booking, DCP, private SAMS eligibility or demand; observe actual paid behavior if the title becomes eligible.

lanes.read: Cultural-sensitivity risk is specific but unquantified: articles report criticism that using sacred Nyepi observance as a horror device is insensitive or misleading.
lanes.strongest_available_evidence: LXPR and IDN Times independently report netizen objections, although neither provides comment volume, representative sampling or measured commercial impact.
lanes.decision_consequence: Track whether controversy becomes rejection, curiosity or remains article-level discourse; do not mistake repeated coverage of the same debate for independent demand evidence.

ai_rating.source_confidence: High on identity and publicity; no independent finished-film verdict.
ai_rating.sams_relevance: Unresolved: public listing does not confirm SAMS eligibility, booking or DCP.
ai_rating.demand_proximity: Low: September 17 is reported, but no presales, paid seats or admissions were captured.
ai_rating.promo_social_strength: Limited: trailer and articles exist; official metrics are absent and the TikTok sample is off-title.
ai_rating.risk_pressure: Moderate but unquantified: articles report Nyepi-sensitivity criticism without measured commercial effect.
ai_rating.actionability: Observe and learn only; measure paid behavior if private eligibility is confirmed.

eligibility.basis: Indonesian title, cast, director, producers and writers with a West Sumatra setting; listed by M-Tix inside the operating window.

coming.meta: Dimas Aditya, Adinda Thomas — DHF/Darihati Films and Right Hand: with Fauzan Nasrul, Ruth Marini and Naura Hakim; directed by Rendy Herpy.
coming.logline: Two travellers ignore a warning and enter a forbidden West Sumatran forest, where the reality-bending terror of Urang Bunian traps them in a fight to escape.
coming.quality: Current-film quality remains unproven: publicity reports positive early responses, but no readable independent review, attributed audience quotation or representative post-screening assessment was captured.
coming.gold: Distinctive regional-horror hook: the Minangkabau legend, West Sumatran setting and forest imagery provide more specific identity than generic supernatural horror, but differentiation is not demonstrated demand.
coming.promo: Visible release-week campaign: special screenings, a Jakarta gala, media and community attendance, creator activity and meet-and-greet elements show organised publicity, not audience quality or paid demand.
coming.social: Small, campaign-shaped social sample: ten recent TikTok results reached 75–3,633 views, with posts dominated by release reminders, screening attendance and direct watch prompts rather than broad organic conversation.
coming.demand: Paid demand is not established: ticket pathways and third-party schedule pages exist, but the bundle contains no presale volume, seats sold, occupancy, sold-out sessions or verified SAMS booking.
coming.risk: Execution uncertainty is the main risk: campaign visibility lacks independent quality and purchase confirmation, while conflicting third-party dates and a geographically questionable cultural claim reduce source reliability.
coming.bet: At owner-confirmed booked sites, Sumatra-linked markets will outperform comparable sites on paid occupancy and admissions per show.
coming.nug: A specific Minangkabau legend and West Sumatran setting give the film a sharper identity than generic supernatural horror; conversion remains unproven.

lanes.read: Local folk horror: two travellers ignore a warning, enter a forbidden West Sumatran forest associated with Urang Bunian, and must escape its reality-bending supernatural terror.
lanes.strongest_available_evidence: Cinema XXI and the captured film overview describe Teddy and Kevin becoming trapped in a forbidden forest linked to the Minangkabau legend.
lanes.decision_consequence: The premise is clear and locally distinctive enough for the room to track whether Minang myth recognition converts into audience response after release.

lanes.read: Recognisable local ensemble, modest commercial draw: Dimas Aditya and Adinda Thomas lead with Fauzan Nasrul, Ruth Marini and Naura Hakim; DHF/Darihati Films and Right Hand are the named producers.
lanes.strongest_available_evidence: Two readable sources consistently identify Rendy Herpy as director, the principal cast, and the Darihati Films–Right Hand production partnership.
lanes.decision_consequence: The package offers familiar faces and regional authenticity, but the captured evidence does not establish a bankable star-driven opening.

lanes.read: Current-film quality remains unproven: publicity reports positive early responses, but no readable independent review, attributed audience quotation or representative post-screening assessment was captured.
lanes.strongest_available_evidence: Radar Jakarta reports positive responses around special screenings and a gala, but supplies no attributable review, score, quotation or negative counterexample.
lanes.missing_fact: A readable independent critic review or attributable, non-promotional audience evidence assessing the finished film.
lanes.decision_consequence: The room should treat the film's atmosphere and cultural texture as a positioning claim, not evidence that the finished experience will retain audiences.

lanes.read: Distinctive regional-horror hook: the Minangkabau legend, West Sumatran setting and forest imagery provide more specific identity than generic supernatural horror, but differentiation is not demonstrated demand.
lanes.strongest_available_evidence: The filmmakers consistently foreground a researched Sumatra/Minang legend, West Sumatran locations and local cultural identity.
lanes.decision_consequence: Use regional recognition as the principal Day-1 learning question while withholding any conclusion about scale until observed audience behaviour exists.

lanes.read: Visible release-week campaign: special screenings, a Jakarta gala, media and community attendance, creator activity and meet-and-greet elements show organised publicity, not audience quality or paid demand.
lanes.strongest_available_evidence: A readable report documents multiple special screenings and a Jakarta gala attended by filmmakers, cast, media, communities and creators.
lanes.decision_consequence: Awareness has received active campaign support, so early social visibility should not be mistaken for organic audience pull.

lanes.read: Small, campaign-shaped social sample: ten recent TikTok results reached 75–3,633 views, with posts dominated by release reminders, screening attendance and direct watch prompts rather than broad organic conversation.
lanes.strongest_available_evidence: The captured ten-post TikTok sample contains modest reach and repeated promotional language; the strongest shown post had 3,633 views, 119 likes, 14 comments and 29 shares.
lanes.decision_consequence: Social proves active seeding and some interaction, but it cannot justify a demand or quality conclusion; organic conversion remains the Day-1 question.

lanes.read: Paid demand is not established: ticket pathways and third-party schedule pages exist, but the bundle contains no presale volume, seats sold, occupancy, sold-out sessions or verified SAMS booking.
lanes.strongest_available_evidence: GoPay provides a purchase pathway, while third-party schedule pages present listings; neither source supplies transaction or occupancy evidence.
lanes.missing_fact: Current presales or seats sold, Day-1 occupancy, and private confirmation of title eligibility and booking at SAMS.
lanes.decision_consequence: Public availability must remain separate from private eligibility; Monday stays observational until owner-confirmed booking and actual purchase behaviour are known.

lanes.read: Execution uncertainty is the main risk: campaign visibility lacks independent quality and purchase confirmation, while conflicting third-party dates and a geographically questionable cultural claim reduce source reliability.
lanes.strongest_available_evidence: Direct Cinema XXI and filmmaker-linked reporting support September 17 and West Sumatra/Minang; some third-party pages instead contain inconsistent dates or describe Kalimantan Selatan cultural relevance.
lanes.decision_consequence: Anchor Monday discussion to the official date and film identity, flag quality and demand as open, and avoid converting noisy public listings into private operating instructions.

ai_rating.source_confidence: High: official identity and September 17 release are consistent; third-party date and geography claims conflict.
ai_rating.sams_relevance: Potentially relevant local release, but public listing does not confirm private SAMS eligibility or booking.
ai_rating.demand_proximity: Low: ticket pathways and listings exist, but no presales, seats sold, occupancy or verified SAMS booking.
ai_rating.promo_social_strength: Modest and campaign-shaped: ten TikToks reached 75–3,633 views amid screenings, gala and direct watch prompts.
ai_rating.risk_pressure: Elevated execution uncertainty: independent finished-film assessment and paid-demand evidence are both absent.
ai_rating.actionability: OBSERVE_LEARN: the useful evidence will be confirmed booking and paid Day-1 behavior, separated from promotional screenings.

what_milo_sees.title: URANG BUNIAN
what_milo_sees.insight: The strongest portfolio hypothesis is regional affinity, not national reach: a specific Minangkabau identity gives URANG BUNIAN a more discriminating paid-behavior test than generic horror awareness.
what_milo_sees.room_question: Among owner-confirmed bookings, is paid Day-1 occupancy and admissions per show stronger in Sumatra-linked markets after timing, capacity and promotional screenings are controlled?
what_milo_sees.strengthens_if: Sumatra-linked markets materially outperform comparable booked markets on both paid occupancy and admissions per show.
what_milo_sees.weakens_if: The apparent lift disappears after exposure and promotional screenings are controlled, or comparable markets perform as well.

title_hypotheses.title: AKAL IMITASI

title_hypotheses.falsifier: The narrow-demand thesis is false if organic admissions per show, excluding confirmed group bookings, meet or exceed the applicable same-site comparable local-new-release benchmark through Day 4 across most owner-confirmed eligible booked sites.

title_hypotheses.title: ISTIMEWA

title_hypotheses.title: TABOO

title_hypotheses.falsifier: The hypothesis fails if TABOO matches or exceeds comparable ordinary releases on paid admissions per show and occupancy through Day 4 without material audience rejection.

measurement.comparison: For genuinely eligible screenings only, compare paid admissions per show through Day 1 and Day 4 with comparable same-week ordinary releases.

title_hypotheses.title: URANG BUNIAN
title_hypotheses.hypothesis: At owner-confirmed booked sites, Urang Bunian's Minangkabau folk-horror identity will produce stronger early audience response in Sumatra-linked markets than in the rest of the comparable SAMS estate.

non_consensus_hypothesis.title: URANG BUNIAN
non_consensus_hypothesis.hypothesis: URANG BUNIAN's narrower Minangkabau identity will produce a clearer paid regional lift than AKAL IMITASI's group-shaped public awareness produces organic lift.

non_consensus_hypothesis.why_stronger_than_alternative: URANG BUNIAN supplies a precise regional mechanism and controlled falsifier, while AKAL IMITASI's larger awareness signal remains vulnerable to organized-group inflation and a disconfirming 5/10 review.
non_consensus_hypothesis.falsifier: The hypothesis fails if owner-confirmed URANG BUNIAN bookings show no controlled Sumatra-linked lift, or if AKAL IMITASI sustains stronger organic admissions per show after group admissions are removed.
